questions.question: -From October 1, 2023, which organisation has introduced the Carbon Border Adjustment Mechanism (CBAM)?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**European Union**__.
 
 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**
 __ 
• The **European Union (EU)** introduced the **Carbon Border Adjustment Mechanism (CBAM)** on **October 1, 2023**, as part of its broader commitment to reducing carbon emissions and addressing climate change. 
• CBAM is a critical policy under the **European Green Deal**, aimed at ensuring that the cost of carbon emissions is factored into the price of imported goods. 
• The mechanism applies to carbon-intensive products such as **cement, aluminum, steel, fertilizers, electricity, and hydrogen**, among others, imported into the European Union. 
• The primary goal of CBAM is to prevent **carbon leakage**, which occurs when companies relocate their production to countries with less stringent climate policies, undermining global climate goals. 
• Initially, the mechanism will operate in a **transitional phase** until 2026, focusing on reporting emissions without imposing financial obligations. Full implementation with a monetary carbon levy is set to begin thereafter. 
 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**
 
• **European Green Deal:** 
• Launched in **2019**, the European Green Deal is the EU's roadmap to make Europe the first **climate-neutral continent** by **2050**. 
• It includes policies targeting **clean energy, sustainable industry, and biodiversity**, along with the CBAM to address carbon leakage. 
• **Carbon Leakage:** 
• Occurs when industries relocate production to regions with **weaker climate policies**, causing an increase in global emissions rather than reducing them. 
• CBAM aims to **level the playing field** by imposing a carbon cost on imports equivalent to the EU’s carbon price. 
• **Implementation Process:** 
• During the **transitional phase (2023-2026)**, importers are required to report the embedded emissions of their goods, but no financial payments are demanded. 
• From **2026 onwards**, importers will need to purchase **CBAM certificates** to account for the carbon emissions of imported goods. 
• **Global Implications:** 
• CBAM has raised concerns among **developing countries** and trade partners, as it could impact their export competitiveness. 
• It encourages other countries to adopt **similar carbon pricing mechanisms** to align with global climate goals. 
• **Comparison with Other Initiatives:** 
• While CBAM is specific to the EU, similar initiatives are being discussed globally to address **carbon emissions in trade**. 
• For example, the **United States** has proposed a **Clean Competition Act** with similar objectives.

questions.question: Who was appointed as the Governor of Manipur in December 2024?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Anusuiya Uikey**__.
 
 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**
 __ 
• **Anusuiya Uikey** was appointed as the **Governor of Manipur** in **December 2024**. 
• She previously served as the Governor of **Chhattisgarh**, showcasing her extensive administrative experience. 
• Her appointment as Governor of Manipur highlights the Government of India's focus on appointing experienced leaders to key gubernatorial roles in northeastern states. 
• Manipur, being a state of strategic importance in the northeast, benefits from her leadership and administrative capabilities. 
• Governors in India are appointed by the **President of India under Article 155 of the Constitution**, and they serve as the constitutional head of their respective states. 
 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**
 
• **Role of Governors in India:** 
• The Governor is the **constitutional head of the state**, acting on the advice of the Council of Ministers headed by the Chief Minister. 
• They have the power to reserve certain bills for the consideration of the President under **Article 200**. 
• The Governor also plays a critical role in ensuring the state’s administration is conducted per the provisions of the Constitution. 
• **Appointment of Governors:** 
• Governors are appointed by the **President of India** for a term of **five years**, but they serve at the pleasure of the President. 
• They can be transferred between states and may also be reappointed for a second term. 
• **Manipur - Strategic Importance:** 
• Manipur is a northeastern state with significant geographical and cultural importance, sharing borders with Myanmar. 
• The state plays a vital role in India's **Act East Policy**, enhancing trade and connectivity with Southeast Asia. 
• It is known for its diverse cultural heritage, including traditional dances like **Raas Leela** and sports such as **Polo**, which originated here. 
• **Key Functions of the Governor:** 
• Appointing the Chief Minister and other ministers. 
• Summoning, proroguing, and dissolving the state legislature. 
• Granting pardons, reprieves, respites, or remissions of punishment under **Article 161**. 
• Ensuring the constitutional machinery of the state is upheld, particularly under **Article 356** in case of a constitutional crisis.

questions.question: Department of Health Research has organized___________ Campaign from 17th September 2024 to 2nd October 2024.

• The **Swachhata Hi Seva Campaign** is a flagship initiative of the **Department of Health Research**, aligned with the **Swachh Bharat Mission**, to promote cleanliness and hygiene across India.

• It emphasizes **community participation** to drive activities such as cleanliness drives, waste removal, and awareness programs aimed at achieving a cleaner and healthier environment. 
• The campaign focuses on ensuring the active involvement of **citizens, schools, businesses, NGOs, and local bodies** to promote sustainable hygiene practices, particularly in urban and rural areas.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**
 __

• It also emphasizes waste management through methods like **solid waste management** and **door-to-door waste collection**.

• **Plastic-Free India Campaign:**

questions.question: The typically Judo platform is of which shape?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Square**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The standard competition platform used in **Judo** is a **square-shaped mat**, commonly referred to as the **tatami**.
 
• The **contest area** is typically **10 meters x 10 meters**, with an additional **3-meter safety area** surrounding it to ensure the safety of participants.
 
• The square layout ensures **equal opportunities** for both players, providing enough space for techniques like **throws, grappling, and groundwork**.
 
• The mats are made of **shock-absorbing materials** to minimize injuries during high-impact throws and falls.
 
• The **International Judo Federation (IJF)** regulations mandate the use of a square contest area to standardize competitions globally, including major events like the **Olympics** and **World Championships**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Judo History:**

 
 
• **Judo** was founded in **1882** by **Jigoro Kano** in Japan.
 
• It emphasizes **leverage, technique, and balance** rather than brute strength.
 
• Judo became an **Olympic sport in 1964** during the Tokyo Games.
 
 
 
• **Tatami Mats:**
 
 
• The mats used in Judo are known as **tatami**.
 
• Traditionally, they were made from **rice straw**, but modern versions use materials like **foam**.
 
• The tatami provides a **non-slip surface** and cushions falls to prevent injuries.
 
 
 
• **Other Shapes in Combat Sports:**
 
 
• **Rectangular:** Used in sports like **wrestling** and **boxing**, suitable for movement patterns in those sports.
 
• **Hexagonal:** Seen in **mixed martial arts (MMA)** to enhance visibility and mobility.
 
• **Circular:** Common in traditional martial arts or **sumo wrestling** to emphasize boundaries.
 
 
 
• **Safety Regulations:**
 
 
• The **International Judo Federation (IJF)** mandates a **3-meter safety area** around the contest area to prevent injuries during high-intensity matches.
 
• The **shock-absorbing mats** are maintained to ensure safe competition conditions.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Judo Belt System:**

 
 
• Judokas progress through a **belt ranking system** (kyu and dan grades) based on their skill levels.
 
• The belt colors range from **white (beginner)** to **black (expert)**.
 
 
 
• **Scoring in Judo:**
 
 
• Points are awarded for techniques like **throws (ippon), pins (osaekomi), and submissions**.
 
• An **ippon** signifies a perfect throw or submission, instantly ending the match.

questions.question: In which year did India won their first Olympic gold medal in hockey?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**1928**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **India won its first Olympic gold medal in hockey in the year 1928** during the Amsterdam Olympics.
 
• The Indian hockey team defeated the **Netherlands (host nation)** in the final with a score of **3-0** to secure the gold medal.
 
• The victory marked the beginning of **India's dominance in field hockey**, as the team went on to win six consecutive Olympic gold medals from **1928 to 1956**.
 
• **Dhyan Chand**, one of the greatest hockey players in history, played a pivotal role in this victory by scoring **two goals** in the final match.
 
• This was the first time India participated as an independent hockey team, symbolizing its emergence as a global powerhouse in the sport.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Dhyan Chand's Legacy:**

 
 
• **Dhyan Chand**, widely known as the "Wizard of Hockey," scored a total of **14 goals** in five matches during the 1928 Olympics.
 
• His birthday, **29th August**, is celebrated as **National Sports Day** in India to honor his contributions to Indian hockey.
 
 
 
• **India's Dominance in Hockey:**
 
 
• India won **six consecutive Olympic gold medals** in hockey from **1928 to 1956**, remaining unbeaten during this period.
 
• During these years, India scored a total of **178 goals** while conceding only **seven**, showcasing its unparalleled dominance in the sport.
 
 
 
• **Other Olympic Gold Medals:**
 
 
• India has won a total of **eight Olympic gold medals** in hockey. These victories came in **1928, 1932, 1936, 1948, 1952, 1956, 1964, and 1980**.
 
• The last Olympic gold medal in hockey was achieved during the **1980 Moscow Olympics**.
 
 
 
• **Field Hockey in the Olympics:**
 
 
• Field hockey was introduced in the Olympics in **1908**, but India participated for the first time in **1928**.
 
• India's early success in hockey helped popularize the sport across the country.
 
• In recent decades, nations like **Netherlands, Germany, and Australia** have emerged as strong competitors in the sport.
 
 
 
• **Important Points:**
 
 
• The **1928 victory** was India's first major international achievement, instilling a sense of pride and unity during the colonial period.
 
• Post-independence, players like **Balbir Singh Sr.** and **Leslie Claudius** contributed to India's continued success in hockey.
 
• Efforts to revive Indian hockey include initiatives like the **Hockey India League** and grassroots development programs.
 
• India's **bronze medal win** in men's hockey at the **2021 Tokyo Olympics** marked a significant step in the sport's revival.

questions.question: Which of the following game is known as the "Gentleman's Game"?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Cricket**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Cricket** is often referred to as the "**Gentleman's Game**" due to its long-standing association with **fairness, respect, and sportsmanship**.
 
• The term originated during the **early days of cricket in England**, where the sport was played predominantly by **aristocrats** and **upper-class individuals**, emphasizing gentlemanly conduct.
 
• **Etiquette** plays a key role in cricket, including respecting the **umpire’s decisions**, applauding opponents’ achievements, and maintaining **discipline** on the field.
 
• The **International Cricket Council (ICC)** actively promotes values such as **fair play** and **mutual respect** among players, aligning with the principles of the "Gentleman's Game."
 
• Although the phrase is traditional, **modern cricket** has evolved to include players from **diverse social backgrounds**, but the emphasis on **sportsmanship** remains central to the game.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **History of Cricket:**

 
 
• Cricket originated in **England** during the **16th century** and became a professional sport by the **18th century**.
 
• The first recorded international match took place between the **USA** and **Canada** in **1844**.
 
• **Test cricket**, the longest format of the game, began in **1877** with a match between **England** and **Australia**.
 
 
 
• **Features of Cricket:**
 
 
• Cricket is played in three formats: **Test matches**, **One-Day Internationals (ODIs)**, and **T20 Internationals**.
 
• It involves two teams of **11 players each**, with roles such as **batsmen**, **bowlers**, and **fielders**.
 
• Key equipment includes a **bat**, **ball**, **wickets**, and protective gear such as **helmets** and **pads**.
 
 
 
• **Global Reach:**
 
 
• Cricket is popular in countries like **India**, **Australia**, **England**, **South Africa**, **Pakistan**, and **New Zealand**.
 
• The **ICC Cricket World Cup**, held every **four years**, is one of the most prestigious tournaments in cricket.
 
 
 
• **Sportsmanship in Cricket:**
 
 
• Players are expected to uphold values like **respect**, **integrity**, and **team spirit**.
 
• Incidents of **sledging** or unsportsmanlike behavior are discouraged and can lead to **penalties**.
 
 
 
• **Important Points:**
 
 
• **Kabaddi:** A traditional Indian sport emphasizing **physical strength** and **strategy**, popular in **South Asia**.
 
• **Badminton:** A racket sport played indoors, originating in **British India**, now globally popular.
 
• **Lawn Tennis:** A global sport played on **grass**, **clay**, or **hard courts**, requiring skill, speed, and strategy.
 
• **Cricket's Cultural Impact:** Cricket has a massive fan base, especially in countries like **India**, where it is considered more than a sport—almost a **religion**. Players like **Sachin Tendulkar**, **Virat Kohli**, and **Don Bradman** are celebrated as icons of the game.
 
• **Cricket Governance:** The **ICC** is the global governing body responsible for organizing international tournaments and ensuring **fair play**. Domestic cricket leagues like the **Indian Premier League (IPL)** have added commercial value to the sport.

questions.question: The shape of Basketball must be _____.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**spherical**__.
 
 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**
 __ 
• The shape of a basketball is **spherical**, ensuring uniformity in its bounce, roll, and gameplay. 
• A spherical design provides a **smooth and round surface**, allowing consistent handling, dribbling, and shooting accuracy. 
• Basketballs are designed to meet **international standards** set by governing bodies like **FIBA** (International Basketball Federation) and the **NBA** (National Basketball Association). 
• The spherical shape ensures the ball rolls predictably and maintains its balance during play, which is crucial for professional and recreational games. 
• Other shapes such as **cylindrical, geoid, or conical** would cause erratic bouncing and movement, making them unsuitable for basketball. 
 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**
 __ 
• **Specific Characteristics of Basketball:** 
• The **circumference** of a standard basketball for men’s games is approximately **29.5 inches** (75 cm), while for women’s games, it is **28.5 inches** (72 cm). 
• Basketballs are made of materials like **leather, composite leather, or rubber**, ensuring durability and grip. 
• The balls are inflated to a standard pressure, typically **7.5 to 8.5 pounds per square inch (psi)**, to maintain their spherical shape during play. 
• **Why Other Shapes Are Unsuitable:** 
• **Cylindrical:** Would lead to uneven bouncing and rolling, making it unsuitable for basketball gameplay. 
• **Geoid:** An irregular shape like Earth's would result in unpredictable movement and bounce. 
• **Conical:** Would not roll or bounce properly, creating challenges in dribbling and shooting. 
• **Historical Context:** 
• The basketball was first used in **1891** when **Dr. James Naismith** invented the game. 
• Initially, soccer balls were used, but later, spherical basketballs were designed specifically for the sport to ensure better control, bounce, and gameplay. 
• **Applications:** 
• Basketballs are used in professional leagues like **NBA, WNBA, and FIBA**, college games, and recreational play. 
• They are also employed in training sessions to develop skills like **dribbling, passing, and shooting**.

• **FIBA Specifications:** 
• Official basketball size for men’s games is **size 7 (29.5 inches)**, while for women’s games, it is **size 6 (28.5 inches)**. 
• **Material Innovation:** 
• Modern basketballs use advanced materials like **microfiber composite leather** for enhanced grip and durability. 
• Some feature **moisture-wicking technology** for better performance in various conditions.

• Provides **tax exemptions** on profits derived from export activities for a specified period.
 
• Allows **single-window clearance** for approvals to reduce bureaucratic delays.
 
• Permits **100% Foreign Direct Investment (FDI)** in the manufacturing sector within SEZs.
 
• Exempts businesses in SEZs from **customs duties, central excise duties, service tax**, and other levies.
 
 
 
• **Objectives of the SEZ Act:**
 
 
• Encourage **export-oriented industries** by creating a conducive environment for trade and commerce.

questions.question: In the context of wear and tear in production process, the replacement investment is same as__________.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**depreciation of capital**__.
 
 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**
 __ 
• **Depreciation of capital** refers to the gradual reduction in the value of physical assets such as **machinery, equipment, and infrastructure** due to factors like wear and tear, obsolescence, and time. 
• **Replacement investment** is the investment made to replace or restore depreciated capital goods. This ensures that the production capacity of a business remains intact and efficient. 
• In the context of wear and tear during the production process, replacement investment is directly related to the **depreciation** of capital goods, as these assets need to be replaced or repaired periodically to maintain operational efficiency. 
• The wear and tear of machinery and equipment is a natural consequence of their continuous usage. This is accounted for as **depreciation** in financial records, emphasizing the need for regular replacement investment. 
• Other options such as **subsidy given by the government, wage of total staff, and entrepreneurship cost** are unrelated to the concept of depreciation or replacement investment. 
 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**
 __ 
• **Depreciation:** 
• It is an **accounting method** used to allocate the cost of a tangible asset over its useful life. 
• Common methods of depreciation include **straight-line depreciation** and **declining balance depreciation**. 
• Depreciation helps businesses account for the **gradual loss of value** of their assets. For example, a machine costing **$100,000** with a useful life of **10 years** will depreciate by **$10,000 per year** under the straight-line method. 
• **Replacement Investment:** 
• This refers to the investment made to replace **depreciated or obsolete capital goods**. 
• Examples include replacing old machinery in factories or upgrading IT systems to enhance productivity. 
• Replacement investment ensures that the **production capacity** and operational efficiency of a business are maintained. 
• **Subsidy Given by Government:** 
• A subsidy is a **financial aid** provided by the government to reduce the cost of goods or services. 
• It is often aimed at encouraging production, investment, or consumption in specific sectors, such as **agriculture** or **renewable energy**. 
• For example, subsidies on fertilizers support farmers and enhance agricultural productivity. 
• **Wage of Total Staff:** 
• It refers to the total payment made to employees, including **salaries, bonuses, and benefits**. 
• It is unrelated to the concept of depreciation or replacement investment, as it pertains to **human resource costs**. 
• **Entrepreneurship Cost:** 
• This represents the cost of resources and efforts invested by an entrepreneur to **start and operate a business**. 
• It includes **opportunity costs**, risk-bearing costs, and organizational costs but does not relate to asset depreciation or replacement investment. 
 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**
 
• **Economic Significance of Depreciation:** 
• Depreciation is a **non-cash expense**, but it is crucial for determining the actual profit of a business. 
• It helps in the proper allocation of resources by accounting for the wear and tear of assets. 
• Businesses often create **depreciation reserves** to fund future replacement investments. 
• **Examples of Replacement Investments:** 
• Replacing outdated machinery with modern, efficient ones in factories. 
• Upgrading software systems to newer versions for improved productivity. 
• Installing new HVAC systems in office buildings to replace older ones. </ul

• The term **'Atman'** is a core concept in the **Upanishads**, referring to the **inner self or soul**, and is distinct from the physical body, mind, and emotions.

• The **Atman** is considered **eternal and unchanging**, representing the true essence of an individual beyond material existence.

• The **Upanishads** describe the Atman as being **identical to Brahman**, the ultimate cosmic reality, emphasizing the unity between the individual soul and the universal spirit.

• Philosophical discussions in the **Upanishads** often revolve around understanding the Atman and its relationship with Brahman, aiming for spiritual liberation (**Moksha**).

• The concept of Atman is central to **Advaita Vedanta**, a non-dualistic school of Hindu philosophy, which posits that realization of Atman as Brahman leads to enlightenment.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__

• **The Upanishads:**

• The **Upanishads** are ancient philosophical texts that form a part of the **Vedas**, the oldest sacred scriptures of Hinduism.

• Major Upanishads include the **Chandogya Upanishad, Brihadaranyaka Upanishad, Katha Upanishad, and Mundaka Upanishad**.

• They focus on spiritual and philosophical teachings, exploring topics like **reality, self, ethics, and liberation (Moksha)**.

• **Relation Between Atman and Brahman:**

• The **Upanishads** assert that the individual soul (**Atman**) is not separate from the universal spirit (**Brahman**).

• Realizing this unity is key to achieving **Moksha**, or liberation from the cycle of **birth and death (Samsara)**.

• **Philosophical Schools of Thought:**

• **Advaita Vedanta:** Proposes non-dualism, where Atman and Brahman are one and the same.

• **Dvaita Vedanta:** Emphasizes dualism, where Atman and Brahman are distinct.

• **Vishishtadvaita Vedanta:** Suggests qualified non-dualism, where Atman and Brahman are distinct yet interrelated.

• **Concept of Moksha:**

• **Moksha** refers to liberation from the cycle of **Samsara** (birth, death, and rebirth).

• Understanding the true nature of Atman as Brahman is essential for attaining **Moksha**.

• **Other Options Explained:**

• **Ritual fire:** While significant in Hindu rituals, it does not refer to Atman.

• **Sacred chant:** Mantras and chants are important in spiritual practices but are distinct from the concept of Atman.

• **Supreme god:** Brahman is considered the ultimate reality, but Atman specifically refers to the individual soul.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

• **Key Terminology:**

• **Atman:** Individual soul or self.

• **Brahman:** Universal spirit or ultimate reality.

• **Moksha:** Liberation from the cycle of Samsara.

• **Philosophical Insights:**

• The **Upanishads** emphasize introspection and self-realization to understand the true nature of the **Atman**.

• They advocate for **renunciation** and **meditation** as paths to spiritual enlightenment.

• **Impact on Hinduism:**

• The concept of Atman forms the basis of various **spiritual practices and philosophies** in Hinduism.

• It influences ethical behavior, encouraging individuals to look beyond materialism and focus on **spiritual growth**.

``

questions.question: Dhruvasena II was the most important ruler of which dynasty?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Maitrakas**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__

• **Dhruvasena II Baladitya** was the most prominent ruler of the **Maitraka dynasty**, which ruled parts of present-day Gujarat, India.

• The **Maitraka dynasty** was established by **Senapati Bhatarka** in the 5th century CE after the decline of the Gupta Empire.

• Under **Dhruvasena II's reign**, the Maitrakas achieved political stability and cultural advancements. He was known for his administrative skills and support for education.

• He was a contemporary of the Chinese Buddhist traveler **Xuanzang (Hiuen Tsang)**, who visited Vallabhi and mentioned the Maitrakas in his accounts, praising their prosperity and governance.

• The **Maitraka rulers** were known for their religious tolerance, supporting **Buddhism, Jainism, and Hinduism**. Their capital, **Vallabhi**, became a renowned center of education and culture.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

• **Maitraka Dynasty:**

• The Maitraka dynasty ruled from the **5th century CE to the 8th century CE**, with its capital at **Vallabhi** in modern-day Bhavnagar, Gujarat.

• Vallabhi became an important **center of education**, attracting scholars from across India and neighboring regions. It was often compared to **Nalanda University** in eastern India.

• The Maitrakas maintained a strong **naval presence**, allowing them to control trade routes along the western coast of India.

• **Xuanzang's Account:**

• The Chinese Buddhist traveler **Xuanzang** visited Vallabhi during Dhruvasena II's reign and noted the region's **prosperity and cultural advancements**.

• He described Vallabhi as a thriving educational hub with a focus on **Buddhist teachings**, comparable to renowned centers like Nalanda.

• **Other Options:**

• **Satavahana Dynasty:** Ruled the Deccan region (modern-day Maharashtra and Andhra Pradesh) from the **1st century BCE to the 3rd century CE**.

• **Chola Dynasty:** A prominent dynasty in **southern India**, known for its maritime trade, temple architecture, and conquests.

• **Kushan Dynasty:** Ruled parts of northern India, Central Asia, and Afghanistan from the **1st to 3rd centuries CE**. Known for their cultural amalgamation and patronage of Buddhism.

• **Decline of the Maitraka Dynasty:**

• The dynasty declined in the **late 8th century CE** due to repeated invasions by the Arabs and the rise of other regional powers.

• The **Arab commander Junaid**, during the early Islamic expansion, attacked Vallabhi, contributing to the fall of the Maitrakas.

• **Legacy:**

• The Maitrakas left behind a legacy of **cultural synthesis, academic excellence, and religious tolerance** in western India.

• Vallabhi's prominence as a center of learning is often compared to ancient Indian universities like **Nalanda** and **Takshashila**.

``
